create.name: Phuntsok Choeling
create.bio:
Phuntsok Choeling, a Tibetan name meaning a place of spiritual abundance, is a small Buddhist centre in Napier in Hawke's Bay, New Zealand. It follows the Sakya school of Tibetan Buddhism and was started by a group of local practitioners under the spiritual direction of Lama Choedak Rinpoche, who visits each year to teach. The centre describes itself as the only Sakya centre in the country and is run as a charitable trust by its members.

Most weeks bring a short morning calm-abiding sit on Zoom from Monday to Saturday, an evening silent sit at the centre on Mondays and a chanted Chenrezig practice on Wednesdays, with a Green Tara puja on the first Sunday of each month; the regular practices are open to all for a koha. Beginners can take a four-week introduction to Buddhism, an eight-week calm-abiding course or a one-day meditation workshop. Each year Lama Choedak Rinpoche leads a weekend retreat in calm abiding and insight and a Vajrayana retreat with empowerments, while senior students lead two rural residential retreats. Recorded public talks are posted on the centre's YouTube channel, and it keeps a lending library of Buddhist books.

courses.title: Calm Abiding Meditation Course
courses.description: An eight-week course in shamatha, the Tibetan practice of settling and steadying the mind, taught at the Napier centre in Lama Choedak Rinpoche's method. The fee includes a copy of his meditation manual; dates are given on request.
